milestones.name: Mac engine images and runtime motion without a desktop capture grant
milestones.bar: Camera continuity expected of Red Dead Redemption 2 and evidence fit for a shipped high-end game: complete native-size images and honest 1x elapsed-time motion, with every omitted sample and observer limit explicit.

items.statement: An opt-in FrameHost tap reads the actual final submitted engine output, preserving normal temporal history, one GPU coordinator and platform lease/loss rules. Disabled capture has no frame copies, readback resources or per-frame allocation.
items.evidence: docs/evidence/render/t2-capture-m0/rework/README.md and verification.json — real-Metal actual-surface RGBA/BGRA correspondence, odd widths/channels/padding, disabled-hook zero allocation and submitted history regressions pass with default and creation-counters features. Copy markers only read the staging buffer; no redraw or game queue owner. Profile Check gates integration.
items.ask: Trace submitted frame to graph copy to image digest; verify no endpoint redraw, second scene render, private game queue submit, drawable bridge or present-lease extension. Run real Metal tests comparing tap pixels with the same output texture, known colour/channel/row-padding cases including odd widths, and submitted history with capture on/off. Preserve existing endpoint-capture tests and Mac M1 loss behavior. Verify disabled-capture zero-allocation and unchanged submitted-history tests run in ./dev check; these required real-Metal tests fail when no device is available.

items.statement: Bounded asynchronous staging and writer queues preserve frame/generation identity through resize, loss, abandon, exhaustion and cancellation; slow or failed output cannot block world/render work or silently complete the evidence interval.
items.evidence: docs/evidence/render/t2-capture-m0/rework/integrated/writer-slow/runtime.json and README.md — expected incomplete: 480 continuing submissions, ticks 0–119, 167 images/313 omissions, 6 GPU/96 CPU peaks within 1 GiB pixel cap, 14.013 s bounded engine drain. Pending loss/replacement, resize, abandonment, stale lease, writer/packaging failure tests pass; failed collection retires its slot and returns CPU lease.
items.ask: Run pending-map loss/replacement and stale-callback controls, ring/writer saturation, disk-limit/write error and bounded-finalization failure. Show finite allocated/queued bytes and continuing ticks/render progress while capture is incomplete; no lost-queue submit or lost-fence wait. Check frames are recycled only after their GPU/CPU leases end, and old generations cannot populate a new session. Include automated incomplete-manifest refusal and decoded raw-spool/PNG hash equality; prove bounded CPU pool ownership through slow disk writes and packaging failures. These regressions run in ./dev check and fail on unavailable required hardware.

items.statement: Before full scenario integration, a measured bounded raw-spool writer sustains the required four-second 1920x1080, 120-record/s workload without overflow; lossless packaging runs after the interval.
items.evidence: docs/evidence/render/t2-capture-m0/rework/final/probe-1 through probe-5/result.json, integrated/pan-1 through pan-5/manifest.json, summary.json — five consecutive 480-record full 1080p120 probes complete with all decoded hashes; service 146.4–297.3 records/s, CPU peaks 4–31/96, full storage flush/drain/deferred packaging recorded. Then five consecutive exact-build pans complete: 480/480, 480/480, 481/481, 481/481, 481/481; no omissions or opportunity skips; integrated service 1.64–2.98 GB/s. All attempts retained, not one selected pass.
items.ask: Run the writer probe on the actual target disk using full raw frame records, declared finite GPU/CPU byte caps and a 16 GiB per-session output allowance. Record write service rate, queue peaks, actual storage/flush behavior, drain and deferred packaging time; verify every decoded image hash. Start with three staging slots/eight CPU buffers in integrated capture. A cached write-acceptance rate alone is insufficient. If the probe overflows, revise the writer before the complete pan; no session-sized RAM queue, live PNG requirement or reduced fidelity may hide failure. Retain commands and measurements; do not call this measured until run.

items.statement: One documented implemented workflow produces exact-build stills, fixed-time sequences and separately labelled real-time offscreen sequences on Metal while the console is locked and Screen Recording permission is unavailable, without requesting a grant.
items.evidence: docs/evidence/render/t2-capture-m0/rework/README.md, verification.json and integrated still/fixed/pan/running manifests — exact corrected binary/source/recipe pinned; locked before/after with denied read-only Screen Recording preflight throughout. Engine stamps live device/presenter generation, consumed common-policy lead and render submission ID. Metal tests prove 7→8 device and 1→3 presenter changes with pending old identity preserved. Still/fixed/pan endpoint parity verified; independent original review separately proved legacy pre/post parity.
items.ask: Rerun retained commands on the actual M3 Max under gpu exclusivity. Inspect recorded lock/permission status, adapter/backend, recipe, source/dirty/build/shader/cooked/parameter hashes and per-frame world/interpolation/history/submission IDs. Verify the headless real-time driver uses actual monotonic elapsed time, the ordinary threaded world/render paths and validated semantic controls. Verify complete source-frame coverage and finalized manifest; no GPU timestamps or OS capture grant required. Preserve fixed-time route/endpoint parity. Unavailable hardware or inability to establish the required locked condition cannot pass. Record the locked condition opportunistically; never lock an active user or unlock by automation. Trace engine output through the ordinary presenter/SurfaceOutput admission path: paused-world semantic camera edits must create fresh submissions with unchanged committed tick and no capture-only admission bypass.

items.statement: The locked-console real-time cooked noon paused-world pan retains complete endpoint holds and coherent scene motion through the ordinary presenter path.
items.evidence: docs/evidence/render/t2-capture-m0/rework/integrated/pan-1 through pan-5 — all five complete, all actual submissions retained; paused tick 0, normal semantic 0→36-degree pan, minimum initial/final pixel holds 1.0027/1.0006 s. PTS, source hashes and full archives validated. Native full frames, adjacent crops and host-time sequence views inspected for coherent rock/ridges, sphere exit and no cut/snap/reversal. Source opportunity counts 480–481 reflect interval termination, not capture loss.
items.ask: Join every submitted image to requested/accepted/submitted controls in the 1920x1080 0-to-36-degree two-second pan at 120 Hz requested opportunities, with one-second initial and final holds. Show fresh submission IDs while the committed world tick stays paused. Account for all opportunities/submissions; capture omissions make the interval inconclusive. A fixed-step route or endpoint redraw cannot pass.
items.inspect: At 1x inspect the full noon pan and both one-second holds: rock and ridges retain coherent relative placement; the sphere follows the authored sweep, including its exit from frame; settled endpoints agree with the declared yaw and scene; no cut, snap or reversal. Record repeats, local holds and gross pauses against host time. Inspect native-size full frames and crops. The Ground E PNG identifies scene and framing only; judge quality against this worded list and the milestone bar, never by matching a target image or awaiting owner image approval. This proves engine runtime motion, not built-in-display smoothness.

items.statement: A locked-console elapsed-time sequence of a running 60 Hz world preserves intermediate-alpha presentation and temporal history.
items.evidence: docs/evidence/render/t2-capture-m0/rework/integrated/running/manifest.json and runtime.json — 481/481, ticks 0–119, 155 strict intermediate-alpha samples, adjacent endpoint records, history epoch 0; engine-consumed lead median 5.895 ms. Native full/crop sequence and PTS-checked 1x preview inspected. Existing alpha-one clamps are exposed (82 among 235 interior-tick records), not hidden or claimed fixed.
items.ask: Join source images to adjacent committed endpoints, interpolation alpha, history and submission IDs in a declared moving-actor scenario at 120 Hz requested opportunities. Show intermediate-alpha samples and no endpoint redraw/history reset; account for gaps and refuse incomplete capture.
items.inspect: Inspect full frames, native-size moving-actor crops and the host-time-preserving 1x sequence through initial hold, running motion and final hold for continuity and interpolation/history artifacts.

items.statement: Explicit diagnostic render and input-dispatch stalls remain visible for their actual elapsed duration; ordinary runs never activate these actions.
items.evidence: docs/evidence/render/t2-capture-m0/rework/integrated/render-stall and input-stall runtime/manifest/previews — actual 255.275 ms render delay creates 261.871 ms image gap; actual 250.036 ms input delay holds 30 identical fresh submissions, then recovery. Source PTS preserved; native sequence views inspected. Requested=start is diagnostic activation and intermediate input edits coalesce; ordinary runs contain no actions.
items.ask: Trace scenario-only actions that delay render-actor work and input dispatch before normal semantic handling, with start/end monotonic times and pinned scenario hash. Verify they are off by default and cannot fire in an ordinary schedule. Compare elapsed delays with image repeats/gaps and PTS; never edit timestamps or compress time to simulate the control. Demonstrate why fixed-time movie smoothness cannot satisfy this item.
items.inspect: At 1x inspect both stall controls and their timelines: the held content or delayed input response must last for the recorded host-time delay and then recover; distinguish capture omissions from actual runtime stalls.

items.statement: Matched capture-on/off runs record observer cost and bounded working-set/disk scaling.
items.evidence: docs/evidence/render/t2-capture-m0/rework/README.md, summary.json and integrated/cost-*/manifest.json — corrected-build OFF/ON/ON/OFF with system load, background snapshot, CPU/disk samples, CPU/scene-GPU/copy-GPU, bytes, memory, queue, write/full-flush/deferred packaging. Copy measured via dependency-ordered GPU upper brackets (ON medians 1.044/1.154 ms). Separate actual CPU samples identify row memmove, stdout scanning, write and wait paths. Whole-child CPU rises 53%/76%; lower step CPU excludes draining and is not a speedup. Scope and timing overhead explicit.
items.ask: Read paired same-build/recipe/workload CPU/GPU/interval/queue/memory/bytes/disk results with run order and load, including deferred packaging and flush costs. Investigate visible hitches, comparable regressions and unexpected scaling under C12 without inventing numeric gates. Captured timing is never the uncaptured baseline.

items.statement: The implemented runbook and consumer handoff state capture modes, provenance, limits, storage retention and the separate attended Mac proof owners.
items.evidence: docs/evidence/render/t2-capture-m0/rework/README.md, docs/CAPTURE.md and per-session retention.json — implemented commands rerun in still/fixed/elapsed/control modes; 16 GiB allowance and free-space preflight; fully decoded archives and selected hashes verified before owned duplicate cleanup. Engine presenter/lead and GPU bracket scope, CPU profiling/load, coalesced input and charged-vs-RSS bounds documented. Mac M2 window/panel/tooling owners remain separate; no Chrome/simulator promotion.
items.ask: Rerun retained documented commands; review C12 and Mac M2 handoff, including M2.3 windowed tap and M2.4 trace investigation. Neither engine PTS nor synthetic opportunities are called compositor swaps, panel refresh or input-to-photon. Verify ASSET-LIFECYCLE records, 16 GiB session allowance, free-space preflight, selected source/time retention and ownership-scoped closeout. Chrome endpoint and simctl interim evidence keeps its explicit limited scope; stronger submitted-motion rows retain their target dependency.

milestones.name: Chrome WebGPU images and runtime motion without desktop capture
milestones.bar: Portable cooked-scene camera continuity expected of Red Dead Redemption 2, with complete canvas sample identity and explicit browser scheduling and surface limits; scene-specific artistic bars remain with the consuming milestone.

items.statement: Chrome captures the actual submitted portable output in fixed-time and elapsed-time modes on hardware WebGPU while the desktop is locked, without OS Screen Recording access or silent software fallback.
items.ask: Rerun the documented cooked-route commands; verify real adapter/backend, browser build/flags and scheduling/throttling profile, exact bundle/content/recipe hashes, clocks and complete frame joins. Do not pass by faking visibility, weakening the existing route refusal rules or asserting headless Chrome is the real visible-tab/display path.
items.inspect: Inspect full-resolution route checkpoints, cuts and 1x moving output for missing content, temporal artifacts and pauses. The manifest names canvas/engine UI included and DOM/browser/native controls excluded.

items.statement: Browser asynchronous capture and artifact export survive loss/resize and slow output with bounded queues and explicit gaps; elapsed-time stalls remain visible and existing lifecycle policy is preserved.
items.ask: Run pending-readback loss/recovery, saturation and injected-stall controls; show the page loop/authority continue, stale captures fail, PTS do not hide delay and missing samples refuse completion. Rerun affected actual-tab/visibility/device-loss consumers; headless canvas proof cannot replace them. Run ./dev check for shared regressions under gpu; additionally retain and rerun the implemented target-specific Chrome command on this target, failing rather than skipping unavailable required hardware. The workspace check alone cannot prove this target row.

milestones.name: iOS simulator engine motion without desktop capture
milestones.bar: Functionally intact cooked scene and normal-speed interaction through simulator lifecycle changes, with honest function-only provenance and no device-speed or physical-display claim.

items.statement: The real simulator foreground route captures engine-rendered stills and elapsed-time motion while the desktop is locked without Screen Recording access, through the shared renderer tap and normal control handler.
items.ask: Rerun the documented route; verify booted model/runtime, host/backend, source/content/recipe and actual world/view/submission IDs and lock state. Separate semantic input from real UIKit touch and mark any OS UI/automation grant row attended with its reason. Required unattended engine-output proof stays open if the target is unavailable.
items.inspect: Inspect complete native-size output and 1x camera/actor motion with initial/final holds and transition frames; identify missing scene content, repeats and continuity breaks. Label simulator function only.

items.statement: Pending captures cancel safely across background/foreground, surface replacement and device-generation recovery without background submission or stale pixels; output remains bounded and gaps explicit.
items.ask: Run lifecycle rows with a capture pending plus saturation/stall controls. Trace foreground/surface leases and generation IDs; prove no background GPU submit, lost-queue work or stale publication, and fresh output after resume. Validate PTS/coverage and incomplete-result refusal; preserve affected iOS route tests and keep physical iPhone evidence pending. Run ./dev check for shared regressions under gpu; additionally retain and rerun the implemented target-specific iOS simulator command on this target, failing rather than skipping unavailable required hardware. The workspace check alone cannot prove this target row.
